content: <thought>Based on the molecular ion (m/z 179.0946) the formula is C10H13NO2 (DBE = 5). The 13C NMR shows a carbonyl carbon at ~166 ppm, six aromatic carbons (≈129–132 ppm), and three aliphatic carbons at 52 ppm (O‑CH₃), 43 ppm (N‑CH₃) and 38 ppm (CH₂ attached to the carbonyl). This pattern fits a phenyl‑CH₂‑CO‑N(Me)OMe fragment, i.e., the Weinreb amide of phenylacetic acid. The corresponding SMILES is **c1ccccc1CC(=O)N(C)OC**.
